facts.claim: Quintana Roo's lodging tax (Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje, art. 8) is 5% of the invoiced value of lodging at hotels and similar establishments, and 6% for apartments, houses and private villas; the guest who pays for the lodging is the taxpayer (art. 7).

sources.title: Quintana Roo Congress: Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje (consolidated text, last reform 23 Dec 2022)

articles/where-to-stay-in-cancun.html: 5% of the room invoice at hotels; 6% for apartments, houses and private villas
The state law makes the guest the taxpayer

facts.claim: The law requires the provider to determine, withhold and pay the lodging tax expressly and separately (art. 11); the tax is never part of the value of the lodging (art. 12); on packages that include food and other services, the base is the lodging element, and at least 60% of the invoice total if the invoice does not itemise (art. 10).

sources.title: Quintana Roo Congress: Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje (consolidated text, last reform 23 Dec 2022)
Quintana Roo Congress: Diario de los Debates, session 34, 15 Dec 2025 (reform of the lodging-tax law, described as aimed at digital platforms)

articles/where-to-stay-in-cancun.html: never part of the value of the room
no less than 60% of the invoice total when the hotel does not itemise

facts.claim: Mexico's general IVA rate is 16% (Ley del IVA, art. 1), applied to the values the law sets, and the IVA is never part of those values.

facts.claim: Visitax is a Quintana Roo fee mandatory for all foreign tourists, with no adult or child rate, paid at visitax.gob.mx or through companies authorised by the state tax authority (SATQ); the state government said in December 2025 that it stays at 285 pesos in 2026 (receipts on the portal in January 2026 reportedly showed 283 pesos).
